text:
The Red Wings have spent most of the season doing the hard part and botching the easy part. They're at 52% of the expected goals, with a goal difference of -3 where their chances say +4.7, and finishing has cost them 9.0 goals. Thursday was a fair summary: a 2-1 home loss to Vegas, decided by Trevor Connelly's winner with 1:42 left.

The other problem is in net. John Gibson has stopped .860 and sits at -6.3 goals saved above expected after +10.1 last season. If you believe that's the real Gibson, Detroit's in trouble; we'd guess it isn't. They're also without Dylan Larkin, listed out with a suspension until around Nov 14. Alex DeBrincat has taken his spot beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson, and Emmitt Finnie has moved onto the top power play. Finnie plays his 100th NHL game tonight and Arvidsson his 700th. "They've finally found it in Emmitt Finnie," Prashanth Iyer of Expected By Whom posted about Detroit's search for a top center, adding "(Only the slightest of hyperbole here)".

Colorado lost 3-2 in overtime to Nashville on Thursday, on a Steven Stamkos winner, two nights after a 7-2 loss in Columbus. Before that, the Avs won three straight by 5-2. Artturi Lehkonen is the hot hand, 11 points (8 goals) in his last ten, and it's backed by real chances: 5.3 expected goals on his own shots against 3.7 usual. Nathan MacKinnon is 85% for a point tonight and 52% for two. Our sleeper is T.J. Hughes, 41% for a point on a line creating 4.10 expected goals per 60.

Our numbers have Colorado slightly ahead, 3.28 to 2.87, which is about as close as a road game in Denver gets.
headline: Detroit is better than its record. Is Gibson?

hunch.text: Detroit's finishing has to turn eventually, and our gut says it starts in Denver. Our numbers lean Colorado; our hunch is a Red Wings win.
